items.title: Vince Giordano interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007

ctx.x: That’s number one. You know I tried to hire Kenny Davern one time when he lived in New Jersey to do a master class. I said Kenny Davern — and we worked together — and I said just bring your clarinet and you, I’ll bring all the recordings, whatever you want to do, and I’ll pay you as much as you want, as long as it’s not a million dollars, to play for my guys. Because what you bring to this music, whether it’s a slow tempo or a fast tempo, the pot is always boiling. There’s this heat, there’s this energy. And he…

They’re old enough but they went and saw Garvin Bushell, they went and saw the real guys from the twenties. They were there and worked alongside of them. And some of that was rubbed off. The newer musicians don’t have that luxury.
